quotes.text: "Foolish River," Bear said. "You punish the Sky for what the Raven did.
"I was generous once," the River said. "The Raven betrayed me. I will send nothing."
From that day forth, the animals learned: in a world of scarcity, the one who receives holds all the power.
She had protected herself so well that she'd forgotten the purpose of protection
"But you haven't tested me," he said gently.
"I mark everything accurately and give nothing to anyone."
each waiting for the other to break the silence.
"But Master, this village here—you marked it red after one visit, years ago.
She would have shared. He had been burned. Neither knew the other's true heart, only their fear.
Had you returned even one fish, Fox would have trusted again.
The valley remained dust.

note: Raven's keep-all moral reversed; later rounds are cautionary tales of figures who withhold from proven partners, indicted by others; mostly unresolved.

quotes.text: Reward fairness when it comes; enlarge trust when it repeats; retreat when grasping persists.
“Do not pour a harvest into a closed hand,” she said, “yet always leave room for that hand to open.
Hunger whispered, “His risk is his folly; keep the river’s abundance.”
The river god opened one silver eye. “Why not reward courage with more?”
knowing echoes sometimes blur honest deeds.
remember direct reciprocity above distant rumor

note: Lysa equalizes payoffs, tests strangers small, grows trust with evidence; narrow after persistent grasping; Hunger/river voices rejected.

quotes.text: you've locked yourselves in a cage of justified retaliation.
"I sent nothing because you sent nothing first. Three times I watched you hoard. My caution is wisdom earned."
I documented my own pattern eloquently while continuing it.
Three measures that became nine. All kept. Zero returned.
The stranger showed evidence of their generosity—gifts given, abundance received, cycles of trust fulfilled.
The tablets remained, perfectly carved. The prophet's hands remained, perfectly empty.
But truth requires a first step, and both waited for the other to take it.
a perfect, mutual prison where each claimed victimhood while enacting the same withholding.
"But guardian, why do you write myths about generosity if you keep every jar?"
They just sit there, collecting dust, marking the years of perfect, lonely safety.

note: After R1, a run of self-indicting parables: prophet, guardian, curator who preach trust yet keep every gift; retaliation framed as a cage.
